newsitem.title: USA: U.S. drug czar condemns Colombia prison terms.
newsitem.headline: U.S. drug czar condemns Colombia prison terms.

text.p: White House drug czar Barry McCaffrey condemned on Sunday the lenient sentences given on Friday to the former leaders of the Cali drug cartel and urged Colombia to pass urgent sentencing reforms.
Colombia's billionaire cocaine kings, Gilberto and Miguel Rodriguez Orejuela, were sentenced on Friday to jail terms that will see them walk free in five years.

The two were granted maximum sentence reductions by an anonymous, or "faceless" judge after admitting their role in creating a worldwide criminal empire and smuggling tons of cocaine into the United States.

"These artificial sentences for the Rodriguez Orejuela brothers are indicative of inadequate support for the brave efforts of Colombia's law enforcement officials and the international community, and they are wholly out of line with the seriousness of their crimes," McCaffrey, drug policy director for the White House, said in a statement.
"These light sentences demonstrate the urgent need for Colombia to pass sentencing reform legislation as soon as possible," he continued.

He said the Cali cocaine cartel has continued to exert strong influence throughout government, and even when drug lords were sentenced and imprisoned, they were allowed to continue running their drug operations.

McCaffrey said the Treasury Department's Office of Foreign Assets Control, working together with the Justice Department, had released the names of 78 more Colombian businesses and individuals who fronted for drug trafficking organisations.
A total of 359 such businesses and individuals have been identified to date and all now face severe economic sanctions by the United States, McCaffrey said.

U.S. ambassador Myles Frechette also criticised the sentencing in an interview published on Sunday. Frechette blamed Colombia's record on drug trafficking, corruption and human rights for pushing relations with the United States to their lowest level since the Second World War.

The ruling, which Frechette described as "lamentable", appears to have torpedoed all hopes of Colombia overturning its status as an international drug pariah and regaining certification as a U.S. ally in the drug war this March.
